title: What does a 40% chance of rain really mean?
text:
Not all rain chances are the same, with some bringing a near guarantee for rain, while others only have a few spotty sprinkles. There is a lot of terminology used to describe these types of rainfall coverage, ranging from isolated to widespread. They all reference a rough coverage area that rain would impact.
Not all rain chances are the same, with some bringing a near guarantee for rain, while others only have a few spotty sprinkles. There is a lot of terminology used to describe these types of rainfall coverage, ranging from isolated to widespread.
They all reference a rough coverage area that rain would impact. Widespread rain means nearly everyone will see rainfall, while scattered is only about 50/50 coverage area. When you hear "there is a 20% chance of rain", it can mean a few different things. Calculating a chance for rain is actually a math equation!
It multiplies coverage of rainfall by percent confidence, or how likely it will rain at all. For example, if 40% of the area is expected to be covered by rain, but forecasters are only 50% sure it will rain or not, that would result in a 20% "chance" of rainfall. Another example suggests 60% of the area will be covered by rain, with about a 90% confidence that it will rain.
That would imply a 54% chance of rainfall, rounded down to about 50%. If 40% of the area will see rain and forecasters are certain it will rain, that would result in a 40% chance of rain. When you read a 30% chance of rain on your phone, just know there are many different ways to get to that number!
That can mean therebe some isolated showers, or only halfway certain in rain, but a good portion of the area will see precipitation. That's why reading further into discussion text associated with a forecast can often help you be more prepared than a simple "chance of rain" percent ever will. Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc.
